chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn A'sham, from some of his companions, who said:

A man had two boys in the womb, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) congratulated him. He said, 'Which of them is older?' He said, 'The one that came out first.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'The one that came out last is the older. Do you not know that she carried that one first, and this one entered upon that one, so he could not exit until this one exited? Therefore, the one that exits last is the older of the two.'
ai.seo_question: How is the birth order of twins determined in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the juristic principle of seniority among twins, ruling that the one who exits the womb last is considered the elder due to the spatial constraint preventing the first-born from exiting earlier. This distinction is crucial in Shia fiqh for determining inheritance shares and marital eligibility, as seniority often dictates priority in these legal matters. The Imam’s reasoning highlights the physical reality of gestation, where the second twin enters after the first, thus remaining in the womb longer and exiting subsequently.
